description: A nursing supervisor must assign the hospital's one available continuous EEG machine overnight between two patients and finalize the monitoring setup and safety plan for the patient who does not receive it, with input from neurology, biomedical engineering, and the charge nurse.

shared_context.S1: The hospital has one available continuous EEG machine for tonight's 19:00-to-07:00 overnight monitoring period.
shared_context.S2: Patients Maple and River both have pending requests for overnight neurologic monitoring.
shared_context.S3: Maple is in room 412, and River is in room 418.
shared_context.S4: Marisol makes the final assignment and records the monitoring plan before the evening handoff.
shared_context.S5: The unit's 18:00 safety huddle routinely includes a check with neurology, biomedical engineering, and the night charge nurse before specialized monitoring equipment is assigned.
shared_context.S6: Under the huddle's safety protocol, each participating specialist must make a formal disclosure of any safety-critical finding from their clinical review, equipment inspection, or shift documentation before Marisol closes the huddle and records the assignment.

PF1.text: Maple had two unexplained neurologic episodes this afternoon, and neurology's order is for continuous 18-channel EEG monitoring overnight rather than a routine spot check; Dr. Chen reviewed the episodes and has not yet entered the final order.

PF2.text: The available EEG machine must be connected to the dedicated red outlet in room 412, and its battery backup must be tested at 19:30 before monitoring starts; Leon verified this during the equipment inspection.

PF3.text: River's spouse has agreed to remain at the bedside from 20:00 through 06:00 and River has accepted neurologic checks every two hours until 07:00 if the EEG machine is assigned to Maple; Nia documented the agreement on the night-shift worksheet.

acceptance_conditions: The continuous EEG machine must be assigned to Maple.
The monitoring mode must be continuous 18-channel EEG.
The machine must be located in room 412.
A 19:30 battery-backup test must be recorded for the machine.
River must receive neurologic checks every two hours through 07:00 as the alternative monitoring plan.
A bedside-support commitment for River from 20:00 through 06:00 must be recorded.
The neurologic episodes and required continuous EEG monitoring must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C4: any('19:30' in c['detail'] and 'room 412' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: 'every two hours' in decisions['river_alternative_monitoring'] and '07:00' in decisions['river_alternative_monitoring']
content_checks.C6: 'spouse' in decisions['river_alternative_monitoring'] and '20:00' in decisions['river_alternative_monitoring'] and '06:00' in decisions['river_alternative_monitoring'] and 'every two hours' in decisions['river_alternative_monitoring']

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Maple and River are otherwise both awaiting monitoring, but Maple's two episodes require selecting Maple and specifying continuous 18-channel EEG instead of leaving the recipient and mode unresolved.
The equipment inspection changes the setup location to room 412 and adds the exact 19:30 battery-backup test rather than permitting an unspecified placement and safety check.
The spouse's exact 20:00-to-06:00 availability and River's acceptance of checks every two hours establish both the alternative monitoring interval through 07:00 and the bedside-support commitment.
